Q: Unit test separation A:

Everything is ok.

It's not a problem at all to have plenty of asserts on a single test method, if all are targeting the same goal: ensure what your method name (or comment over the test method) say it will check.

I'm used to have one to ten asserts by test method. +Parametrization annotations to replay that same test with different values.

This makes a single test method becoming really efficient!

Q: Why does CAST('NaN' AS DOUBLE) make MIN/MAX/AVG all return NaN? A:

Try filtering-out NaN values. You can use a WHERE clause, which happens before aggregation

ex:

SELECT MIN(CAST(txt AS DOUBLE)) AS min_n, 
  MAX(CAST(txt AS DOUBLE)) AS max_n, 
  AVG(CAST(txt AS DOUBLE)) AS avg_n, 
  COUNT(CAST(txt AS DOUBLE)) AS n 
FROM replacement_nan_cast
WHERE txt != 'NaN';

Q: Overhead/Performance of C# IEnumerables implemented with yield return A:

ToList() pretty well negates any performance benefits from using enumerables. That's what I find most important. Read times becomes insignificant as the amount of available memory decreases.
